newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain Islamic bank says offer oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain Islamic bank says offer oversubscribed.

text.p: A new Bahrain-based Islamic investment bank said on Wednesday a $35 million private equity placement offered to investors in Gulf Arab states and South East Asia had so far been oversubscribed by 50 percent.
First Islamic Investment Bank (FIIB) offered the placement to increase paid-in capital to $50 million from $15 million.
"FIIB private equity placement of $35 million has been oversubscribed by 50 percent as of March 25," FIIB said of the offer which closes next month.

"This over-subscription reflects the strong interest in First Islamic among selected high net worth individuals and major financial institutions from the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and South East Asia," it added in a statement.
The GCC, an economic and political alliance, groups Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, Oman, United Arab Emirates and Kuwait.
Saudi Arabia's al-Jomaih group and Kuwaiti investors established FIIB in November last year as an offshore investment bank based in Bahrain.

The statement said the bank was intending to participate with its clients in private equity transactions in the United States and South East Asia in accordance with the Islamic Sharia law which bans the receipt or payment of interest
